 India Today Sports Desk Doha , UPDATED: Nov 20, 2026 15:50 IST India A (IND A) vs Nepal (NEP) Live Cricket Score: All eyes will be on Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as India will begin their title charge in their opening match of the Rising Stars Asia Cup against Nepal. India have a star-studded lineup of ODI hopefuls, looking to leave their mark. ... Read More IND A vs Nepal live score. (AP Photo) 
 Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the Rising Stars Asia Cup clash between India A and Nepal. 
 11 Nov 20, 2026 15:50 IST IND A vs NEP: Abhishek gets going now 
 Abhishek Sharma is beginning to find his rhythm as he takes the attack to Nepal's bowlers.
 The left-hander welcomed Nandan Yadav with a towering six over fine leg before nearly clearing the ropes again with a lofted shot over mid-off.
 However, the pitch has shown signs of holding up, making stroke-making tricky.
 Abhishek had to check his shots on a couple of occasions as the ball did not come on to the bat as expected, suggesting that the surface could pose challenges for the batters.
 Rising Stars Asia Cup, IND A vs NEP: India A (19/0 in 4 ov). Sooryavanshi (9*), Abhishek (9*) 
 Courtesy: Sony LIV 
 Nov 20, 2026 15:42 IST IND A vs NEP: Sooryavanshi breaks the shackles
 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi finally broke the shackles, bringing up the first boundary of India's innings in the third over.
 The young left-hander rocked back and cut Sarraf's length delivery late, beating the fielder at point to find the fence.
 He followed it up with a sliced two over point, showing signs of breaking free after a rather uncharacteristically cautious start.
 Rising Stars Asia Cup, IND A vs NEP: India A (11/0 in 3 ov). Sooryavanshi (8*), Abhishek (2*) 
 Courtesy: Sony LIV 
 Nov 20, 2026 15:38 IST IND A vs NEP: India make cautious start 
 Abhishek Sharma also made an unusually cautious start, struggling to get going against Nepal's disciplined bowling.
 The opening pair went through a phase of nine consecutive balls without scoring a run off the bat, with Abhishek unable to find gaps and Sooryavanshi kept quiet at the other end.
 Nepal's inexperienced bowling attack has managed to frustrate India's explosive opening duo.
 Rising Stars Asia Cup, IND A vs NEP: India A (4/0 in 1 ov). Sooryavanshi (2*), Abhishek (1*) 
 Courtesy: Sony LIV 
 advertisement Nov 20, 2026 15:35 IST IND A vs NEP: Vaibhav makes cautious start 
 Quite uncharacteristic of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has made a cautious start against Nepal.
 After picking up two runs off the first ball following a misfield, the young opener has played out five consecutive dot balls, struggling to find gaps against Pawan Sarraf's disciplined bowling.
 Nepal have managed to keep the explosive left-hander quiet in the opening over, denying him the freedom to unleash his big shots.
 Rising Stars Asia Cup, IND A vs NEP: India A (2/0 in 1 ov). Sooryavanshi (2*), Abhishek (0*) 
 Courtesy: Sony LIV 
 Nov 20, 2026 15:30 IST IND A vs NEP: Abhishek, Sooryavanshi in the middle
 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma are at the crease as India A look to make a strong start with the bat against Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars contest.
 Nepal won the toss and opted to bowl first, hoping to put India A under early pressure. With two explosive left-handers in the middle, India A will be looking to make the most of the powerplay and seize control early.
 Courtesy: Sony LIV 
 Nov 20, 2026 15:27 IST IND A vs NEP: India playing XI
 Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ayush Badoni, Tilak Varna (C), Rinku Singh, Kumar Kushagra (WK), Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav
 advertisement Nov 20, 2026 15:12 IST IND A vs NEP: India bat first 
 The toss is done and Nepal have put India A in to bat first. This means that fans don't have to wait for long to see Vaibhav and Abhishek in action. 
 Nov 20, 2026 14:54 IST Rising Asia Cup live: UAE bundle out Pakistan A for 245
 The defending champions Pakistan A have been bundled out for 245 runs in Doha. Basil Hameed picked up four wickets to rattle the Pakistani batting lineup with four for 37. Shamyl Hussain and Maaz Sadaqat hit fifties but the rest of the batters struggled to make an impact as Pakistan crumbled from 192 for five to being all-out within 47 overs. 
 Screengrab from SonyLiv 
 Nov 20, 2026 14:45 IST IND A vs NEP: Rising Stars Asia Cup format
 The competition features eight sides, divided equally into two groups, with five Full Member nations represented by their A teams and three Associate members completing the line-up. Nepal, in particular, will be an interesting side to watch after showing plenty of promise at the T20 World Cup earlier this year. The 50-over format will now offer a fresh test of their abilities.
 advertisement Nov 20, 2026 14:34 IST IND A vs NEP: INDIA SQUAD
 Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Prabhsimran Singh (WK), Tilak Varma (C), Rinku Singh (VC), Kumar Kushagra (WK), Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav, Arshad Khan, Ayush Badoni. 
 Nov 20, 2026 14:31 IST India A vs Nepal Live Score: Preview
 Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will be the players to watch when India A kick off their Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 campaign against Nepal in Doha on Friday, November 20.
 The tournament's return to the 50-over format gives the two explosive left-handers a different challenge. Both have made a name for themselves with their aggressive batting in T20 cricket, but the competition presents an opportunity to showcase their ability to adapt to the longer format and strengthen their claims for bigger opportunities.
 Led by Tilak Varma, India A will begin their Group B campaign at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium. The tournament, being held in Qatar from November 19 to 29, features eight teams split into two groups. India share their group with Nepal, Pakistan A and the United Arab Emirates, with the top two sides advancing to the semi-finals.
 INDIA A LOOK TO PUT LAST YEAR'S HEARTBREAK BEHIND THEM 
 India have unfinished business in the competition. Their 2025 campaign ended in heartbreaking fashion after Bangladesh A knocked them out in the semi-finals.
 The two sides were tied at 194 before Bangladesh emerged victorious in the Super Over. India will be keen to avoid another painful exit and make a serious push for the title this time around.
 The opening game against Nepal offers them an opportunity to build momentum before a potentially tricky encounter against Pakistan A on November 22.
 ABHISHEK-SOORYAVANSHI COMBINATION IN FOCUS 
 Much of the attention will be on Abhishek and Sooryavanshi, two batters who have become synonymous with fearless strokeplay.
 The pair recently gave a glimpse of what they can produce together, putting on a 133-run opening stand against New Zealand in Wellington. Their assault also helped India register a world-record 118 runs in the powerplay.
 However, the 50-over format will demand a different approach. Both batters will need to show that they can balance aggression with the ability to bat deep and adapt to changing match situations.
 Sooryavanshi, in particular, will return to Doha with fond memories. The Rajasthan Royals youngster enjoyed an outstanding campaign in the previous edition, scoring 239 runs in four matches at an average of 59.75 and a staggering strike rate of 243.88.
 TILAK, RINKU ADD EXPERIENCE TO INDIA A BATTING 
 India A have plenty of firepower beyond their two headline attractions.
 Captain Tilak Varma will be expected to provide stability and lead the batting unit, while vice-captain Rinku Singh brings valuable international experience and the ability to finish games under pressure.
 Prabhsimran Singh and Kumar Kushagra offer wicketkeeping options, while Ayush Badoni adds depth after replacing the injured Rajat Patidar.
 Suryansh Shedge is another aggressive batting option in the squad. With several players capable of changing the course of a game, India A have considerable depth in their batting resources.
 ALL-ROUND OPTIONS AND SPIN COULD BE CRUCIAL 
 India's squad also features a healthy mix of all-rounders and spin-bowling options.
 Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey and Tanush Kotian provide the team with flexibility, particularly during the middle overs. Their ability to contribute with both bat and ball could become important on Doha's surfaces.
 Managing the scoring rate and preventing opposition batters from building partnerships will be among India's priorities in the 50-over format.
 HARSHIT RANA LEADS INDIA'S PACE ATTACK 
 India A have three frontline pace options in Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav and Arshad Khan.
 Rana's experience at the international level makes him a key figure in the bowling attack. Prince and Arshad, meanwhile, will be eager to make an impression and strengthen their credentials.
 India will want their quicks to strike early against Nepal and avoid allowing the opposition to settle into the innings.
 SANDEEP LAMICHHANE THE BIGGEST THREAT FOR NEPAL 
 Nepal will not be short of experience either. They will be captained by leg-spinner Sandeep Lamichhane, whose variations could test India's aggressive batting approach.
 The squad also features established names such as Kushal Bhurtel, Sompal Kami, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Jora.
 Lamichhane's battle against India's power-hitters could be one of the most interesting contests of the opening fixture. India will need to negotiate his spell carefully and ensure they do not surrender control during the middle overs.
 INDIA A EYE STRONG START BEFORE PAKISTAN CLASH 
 India A have the personnel to make a strong impression in Qatar, but their opening assignment against Nepal will require a disciplined performance.
 A victory would not only provide an early boost to their campaign but also help the team build confidence ahead of the Pakistan A fixture on November 22.
 With last year's semi-final heartbreak still fresh, Tilak Varma's side will be determined to make a statement and take their first step towards the Rising Stars Asia Cup title.
